title: Maternal collapse
summary: Sudden collapse or unresponsiveness in a pregnant or postnatal woman.

blocks.heading: Actions
bullets: Call 2222 / put out the emergency obstetric and cardiac arrest call per local protocol; call 999 if outside a hospital setting.
A–E assessment: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure.
If ≥20 weeks gestation (or fundus at/above umbilicus): manual left lateral uterine displacement or full lateral tilt to relieve aortocaval compression — VERIFY exact gestation threshold locally.

If no signs of life: start CPR immediately using standard compression ratios with maternal modifications — chest compressions slightly higher on the sternum, continuous left uterine displacement during compressions.

Consider and treat reversible causes (4 Hs and 4 Ts) plus obstetric-specific causes: haemorrhage, eclampsia, amniotic fluid embolism, high regional block, local anaesthetic toxicity, sepsis, pulmonary embolism, cardiac disease.
If no output within 4 minutes and gestation viable, prepare for perimortem caesarean birth on-site — VERIFY exact timing and activation route per local protocol.
Call for senior obstetric, anaesthetic, and neonatal support immediately.

blocks.heading: What to document
bullets: Time of collapse and time help called.
Interventions performed and times (uterine displacement, CPR start, drugs given, perimortem CS if performed).
